edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: average-risk adults in organised screening programs
edges.mechanism: FIT screening plausibly improves colorectal cancer incidence through a factor-specific pathway documented in the literature, even if the exact size of benefit varies by population and dose.
edges.summary: The anchor for this edge is the 2025 Ribbing Wilén cohort in BMC Public Health, which suggests that fit screening tracks with lower risk or better outcomes for colorectal cancer incidence. Later papers point in much the same direction, so the live uncertainty is usually about effect size or which subgroups carry the signal most strongly.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
